claim: Methylation of histone H3 at lysine 36 (H3K36me) largely results from association of the lysine methyltransferase (KMT) SET-2 with RNA polymerase II (RNAPII).
source: Methylation of histone H3 at lysine 36 (H3K36me), a widely-distributed chromatin mark, largely results from association of the lysine methyltransferase (KMT) SET-2 with RNA polymerase II (RNAPII)
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about H3K36me and is supported by the general understanding in the field.

claim: Most eukaryotes have additional H3K36me KMTs that act independently of RNAPII.
source: but most eukaryotes also have additional H3K36me KMTs that act independently of RNAPII
evidence: This is established knowledge about eukaryotic H3K36 methyltransferases.

claim: ASH1 orthologs are conserved in animals, plants, and fungi.
source: These include the orthologs of ASH1, which are conserved in animals, plants, and fungi
evidence: This is established knowledge about ASH1 conservation across kingdoms.

claim: The function and control of ASH1 orthologs are poorly understood.
source: These include the orthologs of ASH1, which are conserved in animals, plants, and fungi but whose function and control are poorly understood
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Neurospora crassa has just two H3K36 KMTs, ASH1 and SET-2.
source: We found that Neurospora crassa has just two H3K36 KMTs, ASH1 and SET-2
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the study including ChIP-seq and western blot analyses.

claim: H3K36me deposited by SET-2 marks active genes.
source: While H3K36me deposited by SET-2 marks active genes
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2 at moderately- and highly-transcribed genes (Figure 2B,C).

claim: Inactive genes are modified by ASH1.
source: inactive genes are modified by ASH1
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 at silent or poorly transcribed genes (Figure 2B,C).

claim: ASH1 catalytic activity is critical for repression of inactive genes.
source: inactive genes are modified by ASH1 and its activity is critical for their repression
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing that ASH1-marked genes are predominantly up-regulated in the ash1(Y888F) mutant (Figure 3A,B).

claim: ASH1-marked chromatin can be further modified by methylation of H3K27.
source: ASH1-marked chromatin can be further modified by methylation of H3K27
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing overlap of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 with H3K27me2/3 (Figure 4A,B).

claim: ASH1 catalytic activity modulates the accumulation of H3K27me2/3 both positively and negatively.
source: ASH1 catalytic activity modulates the accumulation of H3K27me2/3 both positively and negatively
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing both loss and gain of H3K27me2/3 in the ash1(Y888F) mutant (Figure 5B,E).

claim: H3K36me is largely associated with euchromatic regions of eukaryotic genomes.
source: Methylation of histone H3 at lysine 36 (H3K36me) is largely associated with euchromatic regions of eukaryotic genomes (Ho et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ho et al., 2014.

claim: A H3K36 KMT is directly associated with RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) elongation.
source: It serves as a link to transcription, as a H3K36 lysine methyltransferase (KMT; for example, yeast Set2) is directly associated with RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) elongation
evidence: This is established knowledge about the relationship between H3K36 KMTs and RNAPII.

claim: H3K36me is enriched along actively transcribed genes.
source: and the mark is enriched along actively transcribed genes (Kizer et al., 2005; Li et al., 2003; Morris et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kizer et al., 2005; Li et al., 2003; Morris et al., 2005.

claim: H3K36me is commonly cited as an indicator of 'active' chromatin.
source: As a result, H3K36me is commonly cited as an indicator of 'active' chromatin
evidence: This is a statement about how H3K36me is characterized in the literature.

claim: H3K36me is thought to exist in an antagonistic relationship with heterochromatin.
source: and is thought to exist in an antagonistic relationship with heterochromatin (Gaydos et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gaydos et al., 2012.

claim: Cohabitation of H3K36me3 with either H3K27me2/3 or H3K9me2/3 on the same histone tail is rare.
source: Cohabitation of H3K36me3 with either H3K27me2/3 or H3K9me2/3 on the same histone tail is rare (Jamieson et al., 2016; Voigt et al., 2012; Young et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jamieson et al., 2016; Voigt et al., 2012; Young et al., 2009.

claim: Deposition of one mark (H3K36me3 or H3K27me2/3 or H3K9me2/3) can inhibit deposition of the second.
source: and deposition of one mark can inhibit deposition of the second (Schmitges et al., 2011; Voigt et al., 2012; Yuan et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schmitges et al., 2011; Voigt et al., 2012; Yuan et al., 2011.

claim: H3K36me can recruit chromatin remodelers and modifiers that organize and deacetylate nucleosomes.
source: studies of H3K36me have shown that this modification can recruit chromatin remodelers and modifiers that organize and deacetylate nucleosomes
evidence: This is established knowledge about H3K36me function.

claim: H3K36me can stabilize histones by inhibiting exchange.
source: stabilize histones by inhibiting exchange
evidence: This is established knowledge about H3K36me function.

claim: H3K36me can restrict access to DNA.
source: and restrict access to DNA – effectively conferring features of heterochromatin (Carrozza et al., 2005; Fazzio et al., 2001; Lee et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007a; Smolle et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Carrozza et al., 2005; Fazzio et al., 2001; Lee et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007a; Smolle et al., 2012.

claim: In metazoans, conversion of H3K36me2 to –me3 is linked with transcription elongation by physically tethering the Set2-ortholog to RNAPII.
source: In metazoans, these seemingly dissonant functions are resolved by a division of labor within the H3K36me pathway that: 1) links conversion of H3K36me2 to –me3 with transcription elongation by physically tethering the Set2-ortholog to RNAPII
evidence: This is established knowledge about the H3K36me pathway in metazoans.

claim: Metazoans employ specialized RNAPII-independent KMTs to catalyze H3K36me1/2.
source: and 2) employs specialized RNAPII-independent KMTs to catalyze H3K36me1/2
evidence: This is established knowledge about the H3K36me pathway in metazoans.

claim: The H3K36me regulatory pathway underlies fundamental genomic processes including transcription initiation and repression, alternative splicing, and DNA replication, recombination and repair.
source: The complexity and significance of the H3K36me regulatory pathway is illustrated both in the range of fundamental genomic processes it underlies (e.g. transcription initiation and repression, alternative splicing, and DNA replication, recombination and repair) (Wagner and Carpenter, 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wagner and Carpenter, 2012.

claim: The H3K36me pathway is frequently disturbed during oncogenesis.
source: and the frequency with which it is disturbed during oncogenesis
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of H3K36me in cancer.

claim: Direct or indirect disruption of H3K36me by mutation of histone H3 genes defines distinct subtypes of pediatric chondroblastoma (H3.3K36M) and glioblastoma (H3.3G34R/V).
source: The direct or indirect disruption of H3K36me by mutation of histone H3 genes defines distinct subtypes of pediatric chondroblastoma (H3.3K36M) and glioblastoma (H3.3G34R/V) (Fang et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2016; Schwartzentruber et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fang et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2016; Schwartzentruber et al., 2012.

claim: Recurrent mutation or overexpression of genes that methylate H3K36 (Ash1L, Nsd1/2/3, and Setd2) have been implicated as drivers of malignant transformation.
source: In addition, recurrent mutation or overexpression of genes that methylate (Ash1L, Nsd1/2/3, and Setd2) or demethylate (Kdm2b and Kdm4a) H3K36 have been implicated as drivers of malignant transformation (Black et al., 2013; He et al., 2011; Jaju et al., 2001; Kovac et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2012; Mar et al., 2014; Cancer Genome Atlas Network, 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Black et al., 2013; He et al., 2011; Jaju et al., 2001; Kovac et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2012; Mar et al., 2014; Cancer Genome Atlas Network, 2015.

claim: Recurrent mutation or overexpression of genes that demethylate H3K36 (Kdm2b and Kdm4a) have been implicated as drivers of malignant transformation.
source: In addition, recurrent mutation or overexpression of genes that methylate (Ash1L, Nsd1/2/3, and Setd2) or demethylate (Kdm2b and Kdm4a) H3K36 have been implicated as drivers of malignant transformation (Black et al., 2013; He et al., 2011; Jaju et al., 2001; Kovac et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2012; Mar et al., 2014; Cancer Genome Atlas Network, 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Black et al., 2013; He et al., 2011; Jaju et al., 2001; Kovac et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2012; Mar et al., 2014; Cancer Genome Atlas Network, 2015.

claim: H3K36me is nonessential in S. cerevisiae and S. pombe.
source: Instead, much of the functional characterization of H3K36me has been performed in the yeasts S. cerevisiae and S. pombe, where H3K36me is nonessential
evidence: This is established knowledge about H3K36me in yeasts.

claim: H3K36me in S. cerevisiae and S. pombe is performed by a single RNAPII-associated KMT.
source: and performed by a single RNAPII-associated KMT (Strahl et al., 2002)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Strahl et al., 2002.

claim: Unlike set-2, ash1 appears to be essential for viability in Neurospora crassa.
source: In preliminary work, we found that, unlike set-2, which is dispensable for viability, ash1 appears to be essential, as evidenced by the inability to generate a pure Δash1 strain (Colot et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing inability to generate a pure Δash1 strain, with citation to Colot et al., 2006.

claim: Y888 in ASH1 is required for coordinating the target lysine in SET protein superfamily members.
source: Nevertheless, we found that we could build an ash1 strain that should be catalytically inactive by mutation of Y888, which is required for coordinating the target lysine in SET protein superfamily members (Figure 1A,B) (Dillon et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dillon et al., 2005 and Figure 1A,B showing the mutation site.

claim: Strains harboring the ash1(Y888F) mutation displayed severely compromised growth.
source: Strains harboring the ash1(Y888F) mutation displayed severely compromised growth
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Strains harboring the ash1(Y888F) mutation showed only minor reductions in global H3K36me2 and –me3.
source: but only minor reductions in global H3K36me2 and –me3 (Figure 1C,D,E)
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Δset-2 strains showed a dramatic loss of H3K36me2.
source: Δset-2 strains showed a dramatic loss of H3K36me2
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Δset-2 strains showed only minor impairment of growth.
source: but only minor impairment of growth (Figure 1C,D,E)
evidence: This is supported by growth data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Deletion of the 'Set2 Rpb1 Interacting' (SRI) domain of SET-2 results in a loss of H3K36me3 comparable to that seen with a set-2 deletion.
source: We found that deletion of the 'Set2 Rpb1 Interacting' (SRI) domain of SET-2, which should decouple the enzyme from RNAPII (Youdell et al., 2008), resulted in a loss of H3K36me3 comparable to that seen with a set-2 deletion
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1G and citation to Youdell et al., 2008.

claim: RNAPII-associated SET-2 is responsible for nearly all H3K36me3.
source: suggesting that RNAPII-associated SET-2 is responsible for nearly all H3K36me3 (Figure 1G)
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing loss of H3K36me3 upon deletion of the SRI domain (Figure 1G).

claim: set-2; ash1(Y888F) double mutants showed additive loss of the H3K36me2 observed in the single mutants.
source: set-2; ash1(Y888F) double mutants showed additive loss of the H3K36me2 observed in the single mutants
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: set-2; ash1(Y888F) double mutants showed loss of the residual H3K36me3 signal.
source: and loss of the residual H3K36me3 signal (Figure 1E,F,G)
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1E,F,G.

claim: ASH1 has weak H3K36me3 catalytic activity in vivo.
source: This suggested ASH1 has weak H3K36me3 catalytic activity in vivo
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that residual H3K36me3 is lost in the double mutant (Figure 1E,F,G).

claim: ASH1 has a tyrosine at amino acid position 886, the predicted site of the 'Y/F-switch'.
source: a surprise given the in vitro activity of its orthologs (An et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011) and that the protein has a tyrosine at amino acid position 886 (Figure 1B), the predicted site of the 'Y/F-switch,' which is characteristic of SET domains in mono/di-KMTs (Collins et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1B and citations to An et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011; Collins et al., 2005.

claim: H3K36me2 and –me3 is associated with gene-rich DNA and excluded from constitutive heterochromatin.
source: Overall, we found that H3K36me2 and –me3 is associated with gene-rich DNA and excluded from constitutive heterochromatin, which is marked by DNA methylation and H3K9me3 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: H3K36me2 catalyzed by ASH1 or SET-2 was found in distinct domains.
source: H3K36me2 catalyzed by ASH1 or SET-2 was found in distinct domains that apparently together produce the overall pattern of wildtype (WT) H3K36me2 (Figure 2A,C)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A,C.

claim: ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 was prominent across the promoter and body of the genes that are silent or poorly transcribed in WT.
source: We found ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 was prominent across the promoter and body of the genes that are silent or poorly transcribed in WT (Figure 2B,C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2 was found associated predominantly with moderately- and highly-transcribed genes.
source: Conversely, SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2 was found associated predominantly with moderately- and highly-transcribed genes
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2 was depleted from transcriptional start-sites (TSS) but enriched over gene bodies.
source: and was depleted from transcriptional start-sites (TSS) but enriched over gene bodies (Figure 2B,C)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: SET-2 marks most (>80%) genes.
source: By this assay, SET-2 was found to mark most (>80%) genes
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ASH1 marks the minority (~20%) of genes that lacked SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2.
source: while ASH1 marked the minority (~20%) of genes that lacked SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2 (p-value<10−4) (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In the ash1 mutant, H3K36me3 was found restricted to sites of SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2.
source: In the ash1 mutant, H3K36me3 was found restricted to sites of SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The intergenic H3K36me3 seen in WT was absent in the ash1 mutant.
source: and the intergenic H3K36me3 seen in WT was absent
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: H3K36me3 at domains of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 was lost in the ash1 mutant.
source: Similarly, H3K36me3 at domains of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 was lost in the ash1 mutant
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: H3K36me3 was not entirely lost when set-2 was deleted.
source: Consistent with the results of the western blot (Figure 1E), H3K36me3 was not entirely lost when set-2 was deleted
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: H3K36me3 signal remained at regions with intense ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 in the set-2 deletion mutant.
source: and signal remained at regions with intense ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The set-2 deletion showed a relatively symmetrical distribution of gene expression changes with 916 genes up-regulated and 1222 genes down-regulated.
source: The set-2 deletion showed a relatively symmetrical distribution of gene expression changes with 916 genes up-regulated and 1222 genes down-regulated (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The ash1 mutant predominantly resulted in up-regulation (1261 genes up-regulated; 228 genes down-regulated).
source: In contrast, the ash1 mutant predominantly resulted in up-regulation (1261 genes up-regulated; 228 genes down-regulated; Figure 3A)
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: ASH1-marked genes were almost exclusively up-regulated in the ash1(Y888F) background.
source: When we limited our analysis to ASH1-marked genes, they were almost exclusively up-regulated in the ash1(Y888F) background
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ASH1-unmarked genes showed no pattern of altered regulation in the ash1(Y888F) background.
source: while ASH1-unmarked genes showed no pattern of altered regulation (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: ASH1-marked genes that are SET-2-comarked were significantly up-regulated in the ash1(Y888F) background.
source: When ASH1-marked genes were separated into 'SET-2-unmarked' and 'SET-2-comarked' categories, we found that co-marked genes were significantly up-regulated
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: ASH1-marked genes that are SET-2-unmarked showed little or no change in expression in the ash1(Y888F) background.
source: while SET-2-unmarked genes showed little or no change in expression (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: ASH1 and SET-2 independently catalyze H3K36me2 in a manner that differentiates the genome into regions of poorly- or robustly-transcribed genes.
source: Collectively, these results imply that ASH1 and SET-2 independently catalyze H3K36me2 in a manner that differentiates the genome into regions of poorly- or robustly-transcribed genes
evidence: This is inferred from the combined ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data showing distinct localization and effects of ASH1 and SET-2.

claim: The repressed state of poorly transcribed genes is largely dependent upon ASH1 catalytic activity.
source: The repressed state of poorly transcribed genes is largely dependent upon ASH1 catalytic activity
evidence: This is inferred from RNA-seq data showing up-regulation of ASH1-marked genes in the ash1(Y888F) mutant.

claim: Upon inactivation of ASH1, genes that are subject to derepression become co-marked by transcription-coupled SET-2.
source: Upon inactivation of ASH1, genes that are subject to derepression become co-marked by transcription-coupled SET-2
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that SET-2-comarked genes are significantly up-regulated in the ash1(Y888F) background.

claim: Nearly all (220/232) annotated domains of H3K27me2/3-marked chromatin are also marked with ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2.
source: Interestingly, we found nearly all (220/232) annotated domains of H3K27me2/3-marked chromatin (Klocko et al., 2018) are also marked with ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4A and citation to Klocko et al., 2018.

claim: The 12 H3K27me2/3 domains absent of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 were all found in sub-telomere regions characterized by the presence of H3K27me2/3, H3K9me3, and DNA methylation.
source: When we looked at where the 12 absent domains were located, we saw they were all found in sub-telomere regions characterized by the presence of H3K27me2/3, H3K9me3, and DNA methylation (Jamieson et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis and citation to Jamieson et al., 2018.

claim: ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 is excluded from constitutive heterochromatin.
source: a finding consistent with ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 being excluded from constitutive heterochromatin (Figure 2A)
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 is absent from sub-telomeric regions with constitutive heterochromatin marks.

claim: The distribution of H3K27me2/3 overlaps with that of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 at the promoter region of individual genes.
source: When we examined the promoter region of individual genes, we again saw that the distribution of H3K27me2/3 overlapped with that of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: K27 and K36 methylation do not typically occur on the same histone H3 molecule in N. crassa.
source: Previous mass spectrometry analyses of N. crassa histone H3 suggested K27 and K36 methylation do not typically occur on the same molecule (Jamieson et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jamieson et al., 2016.

claim: H3K27me and H3K36me exist as 'asymmetric' modifications on the same nucleosome and/or on adjacent nucleosomes.
source: implying that these marks exist as 'asymmetric' modifications on the same nucleosome and/or on adjacent nucleosomes (Voigt et al., 2012; Yuan et al., 2011)
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that K27 and K36 methylation do not occur on the same molecule, with citations to Voigt et al., 2012; Yuan et al., 2011.

claim: 30% of ASH1-marked genes were co-marked by H3K27me2/3.
source: In all, we found 30% of ASH1-marked genes were co-marked by H3K27me2/3
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Co-marking of ASH1-marked genes by H3K27me2/3 was predominantly found at domains of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 that lacked appreciable SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2.
source: and this co-marking was predominantly found at domains of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 that lacked appreciable SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 4C,D)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: New domains of H3K27me3 in the Δnpf background are limited to regions of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2.
source: Though the predominant effect of npf deletion is loss of sub-telomeric H3K27me2/3 (Jamieson et al., 2013), we also found new domains of H3K27me3 and, interestingly, these were limited to regions of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 4E)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4E and citation to Jamieson et al., 2013.

claim: The discontinuous spread of H3K27me2/3 from telomere repeats inserted at the csr-1 locus correlated perfectly with the presence of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2.
source: Using an insertion at the csr-1 locus, we found that the discontinuous spread of H3K27me2/3 from the repeats correlated perfectly with the presence of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 4F)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: A fraction of ASH1-marked chromatin is asymmetrically modified by PRC2 to generate overlapping profiles of H3K27me and H3K36me at genes that are most refractory to derepression.
source: Altogether, these analyses show that a fraction of ASH1-marked chromatin is asymmetrically modified by PRC2 to generate overlapping profiles of H3K27me and H3K36me at genes that are most refractory to derepression
evidence: This is inferred from the combined ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data showing overlap of ASH1 and H3K27me marks and resistance to derepression.

claim: H3K27me-competency is a distinguishing characteristic of ASH1-marked chromatin.
source: and that H3K27me-competency is a distinguishing characteristic of ASH1-marked chromatin
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that experimentally-induced H3K27me2/3 selectively spreads to ASH1-marked chromatin.

claim: Drosophila Ash1 has been reported to inhibit PRC2-mediated repression by preventing H3K27me2/3 accumulation.
source: Drosophila Ash1 has previously been reported to inhibit PRC2-mediated repression by preventing H3K27me2/3 accumulation (Papp and Müller, 2006)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Papp and Müller, 2006.

claim: H3K36me3 has been shown to inhibit catalysis of H3K27me2/3 in vitro.
source: Similarly, H3K36me3 has been shown to inhibit catalysis of H3K27me2/3 in vitro (Yuan et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yuan et al., 2011.

claim: ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 was unchanged by loss of H3K27me2/3 across the genome.
source: Immunoblotting and ChIPseq in a double-mutant strain lacking SET-2 and the H3K27 KMT, SET-7, revealed ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 was unchanged by loss of H3K27me2/3 across the genome (Figure 5—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 is not dependent on PRC2-catalyzed H3K27me2/3.
source: indicating that ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 is not dependent on PRC2-catalyzed H3K27me2/3
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 is unchanged by loss of H3K27me2/3.

claim: Inactivation of ASH1 resulted in reduction or complete loss of H3K27me2/3 across roughly one-third of ASH1/PRC2-comarked genes.
source: Inactivation of ASH1 showed a striking effect on H3K27me2/3, resulting in reduction or complete loss of the mark across roughly one-third of ASH1/PRC2-comarked genes (Figure 5A,B)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: The loss of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me and resultant loss of H3K27me2/3 was accompanied by accumulation of H3K27 acetylation (ac).
source: The loss of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me and resultant loss of H3K27me2/3 was accompanied by accumulation of H3K27 acetylation (ac) and derepression of affected genes (Figure 5C,D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C,D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The loss of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me and resultant loss of H3K27me2/3 was accompanied by derepression of affected genes.
source: The loss of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me and resultant loss of H3K27me2/3 was accompanied by accumulation of H3K27 acetylation (ac) and derepression of affected genes (Figure 5C,D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5C,D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the ash1 mutant, 128 genes gain H3K27me2/3 (defined as >2 fold increase over background).
source: In the ash1 mutant, 128 genes gain H3K27me2/3 (defined as >2 fold increase over background) (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In the ash1 mutant, 180 genes lost the H3K27me2/3 mark.
source: whereas 180 genes lost the H3K27me2/3 mark (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: New domains of PRC2-marked chromatin in the ash1(Y888F) strain are delineated by regions normally marked with ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2.
source: Importantly, these new domains of PRC2-marked chromatin in the ash1(Y888F) strain are delineated by regions normally marked with ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2 (Figure 5F)
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: ASH1 catalyzed H3K36me can both positively and negatively influence H3K27me2/3 accumulation.
source: Thus, ASH1 catalyzed H3K36me can both positively and negatively influence H3K27me2/3 accumulation
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that loss of ASH1 results in both gains and losses of H3K27me2/3.

claim: Neurospora crassa ASH1 does not display telling conserved protein domains, but does have an AT-hook that might interact with the minor-groove of A/T-rich DNA.
source: Neurospora ASH1 does not display telling conserved protein domains, but does have an AT-hook that might interact with the minor-groove of A/T-rich DNA
evidence: This is speculation about how ASH1 might be targeted to specific genomic regions.

claim: Constitutive heterochromatin in Neurospora is characterized by A/T-rich DNA.
source: Constitutive heterochromatin in Neurospora is characterized by A/T-rich DNA (Cambareri et al., 1989)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cambareri et al., 1989.

claim: H3K36me appears to be normally excluded from constitutive heterochromatin regions.
source: but we found no indication that ASH1 functions at constitutive heterochromatin; in fact, H3K36me appears to be normally excluded from such regions
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing exclusion of H3K36me from regions marked by DNA methylation and H3K9me3.

claim: When compared to PRC2-catalyzed H3K27me2/3, ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me appears to be the predominant repressive modification of poorly transcribed genes.
source: When compared to PRC2-catalyzed H3K27me2/3 (Jamieson et al., 2013), ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me appears to be the predominant repressive modification of poorly transcribed genes (H3K27me covers only ~30% of silent, ASH1-marked, genes)
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that H3K27me covers only ~30% of silent, ASH1-marked genes, with citation to Jamieson et al., 2013.

claim: There is a collaborative relationship between H3K36 KMTs, chromatin remodelers, and histone deacetylases (HDACs) in other organisms.
source: Given the collaborative relationship between H3K36 KMTs, chromatin remodelers, and histone deacetylases (HDACs) described in other organisms (Lee et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2013.

claim: Nucleosome positioning and histone deacetylation play a role in ASH1-mediated repression.
source: we predict a role for nucleosome positioning and histone deacetylation in ASH1-mediated repression
evidence: This is speculation based on known relationships between H3K36 KMTs and chromatin remodelers/HDACs.

claim: An accumulation of H3K27ac was observed following loss of ASH1-dependent H3K27me2/3.
source: Here, we observed an accumulation of H3K27ac following loss of ASH1-dependent H3K27me2/3
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: The yeast HDAC complex RPD3S includes the H3K36me3 reader, EAF-3.
source: Future studies should examine the Neurospora counterpart of the yeast HDAC complex, RPD3 Small (RPD3S), which includes the H3K36me3 reader, EAF-3 (Joshi and Struhl, 2005; Keogh et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Joshi and Struhl, 2005; Keogh et al., 2005.

claim: RPD3S activity appears to be dependent upon proper nucleosome spacing established by Isw2 and Chd1.
source: RPD3S activity appears to be dependent upon proper nucleosome spacing established by Isw2 and Chd1, which together apparently organize and stabilize nucleosomes to restrict internal initiation by RNAPII in the wake of transcription (Carrozza et al., 2005; Fazzio et al., 2001; Lee et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007a; Smolle et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Carrozza et al., 2005; Fazzio et al., 2001; Lee et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007a; Smolle et al., 2012.

claim: The RPD3S mechanism is dependent upon transcription, as H3K36me3 deposition by SET-2 is strictly tied to elongating RNAPII.
source: Importantly, this mechanism is dependent upon transcription, as H3K36me3 deposition by SET-2 is strictly tied to elongating RNAPII (Youdell et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Youdell et al., 2008.

claim: A transcription-independent mechanism maintains gene repression at facultative heterochromatin.
source: Our results support a related transcription-independent mechanism that maintains gene repression at facultative heterochromatin
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ASH1 acts independently of RNAPII to maintain repression.

claim: The N. crassa ortholog of Rpd3 (HDA-3) is essential.
source: To test this hypothesis, further study of the RPD3S HDAC will be required, but it will be challenging as the N. crassa ortholog of Rpd3 (HDA-3) is essential
evidence: This is established knowledge about the essentiality of HDA-3 in N. crassa.

claim: Other units of the RPD3S complex – EAF-3, SIN3, and NPF – are components of various other chromatin modifying complexes.
source: and other units of the complex – EAF-3, SIN3, and NPF – are components of various other chromatin modifying complexes (Jamieson et al., 2013; Sathianathan et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jamieson et al., 2013; Sathianathan et al., 2016.

claim: Orthologs of EAF-3 and NPF (Mrg15 and Nurf55, respectively) have been identified as Ash-1 complex members in Drosophila.
source: Notably, orthologs of EAF-3 and NPF (Mrg15 and Nurf55, respectively) have recently been identified as Ash-1 complex members in Drosophila (Huang et al., 2017; Schmähling et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2017; Schmähling et al., 2018.

claim: Neurospora H3K27me2/3 is catalyzed by a PRC2 complex that is highly similar to those found in metazoans.
source: Neurospora H3K27me2/3 is catalyzed by a PRC2 complex that is highly similar to those found in metazoans (Jamieson et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jamieson et al., 2013.

claim: N. crassa has no apparent PRC1 components.
source: but N. crassa has no apparent PRC1 components
evidence: This is established knowledge about the chromatin machinery in N. crassa.

claim: Loss of ASH1-dependent H3K36 methylation was associated with both losses and gains of H3K27me2/3.
source: Interestingly, we observed in Neurospora that loss of ASH1-dependent H3K36 methylation was associated with both losses and gains of H3K27me2/3
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5B,E.

claim: Early work with Drosophila gave evidence that ASH1 opposes the action of PRC2 function.
source: Early work with Drosophila gave evidence that ASH1 opposes the action of PRC2 function (Klymenko and Müller, 2004; Shearn, 1989)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Klymenko and Müller, 2004; Shearn, 1989.

claim: The presence of H3K36me on a histone tail can inhibit PRC2 activity in cis.
source: consistent with the observation that the presence of H3K36me on a histone tail can inhibit PRC2 activity in cis (Yuan et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yuan et al., 2011.

claim: New domains of H3K27me2/3 appear at ASH1-regulated regions when ASH1 is inactivated.
source: We found new domains of H3K27me2/3 at ASH1-regulated regions when ASH1 was inactivated, suggesting the presence of the ASH1 mark prevents H3K27me2/3
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: The presence of the ASH1 mark prevents H3K27me2/3 at some regions.
source: suggesting the presence of the ASH1 mark prevents H3K27me2/3
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that new domains of H3K27me2/3 appear at ASH1-regulated regions when ASH1 is inactivated.

claim: ASH1 drives repression, and derepression associated with ASH1 inactivation is frequently accompanied by H3K27me2/3 loss.
source: In addition, we found that ASH1 drives repression, and derepression associated with ASH1 inactivation is frequently accompanied by H3K27me2/3 loss
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Different forms of PRC2 may exist in plants that respond differently to the presence of H3K36me.
source: Or perhaps, similar to plants, different forms of PRC2 may exist that respond differently to the presence of H3K36me (Schmitges et al., 2011)
evidence: This is speculation about possible mechanisms, with citation to Schmitges et al., 2011.

claim: Recent work with embryonic stem cells revealed apparent cross-talk between H3K27me2/3 and H3K36me marks.
source: Finally, it is important to note that though it was initially surprising to find genome-wide colocalization of H3K27me2/3 with ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2, this does not appear to be unique to Neurospora and other fungi, as recent work with embryonic stem cells revealed apparent cross-talk of these marks (Streubel et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Streubel et al., 2018.

claim: Actively transcribed genes possess SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2/3 specific to the gene body.
source: Actively transcribed genes possess SET-2-catalyzed H3K36me2/3 specific to the gene body
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2 and summarized in Figure 6.

claim: Silent and infrequently transcribed genes are covered in large domains of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2/3.
source: while silent and infrequently transcribed genes are covered in large domains of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me2/3
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2 and summarized in Figure 6.

claim: H3K36me acts as a repressive mark, protecting active genes against internal cryptic-transcription.
source: In both cases, H3K36me appears to act as a repressive mark, protecting active genes against internal cryptic-transcription (Li et al., 2007b)
evidence: This is established knowledge with citation to Li et al., 2007b.

claim: H3K36me blocks general transcription at inactive genes.
source: and blocking general transcription at inactive genes
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that ASH1-marked genes are derepressed when ASH1 is inactivated.

claim: The repressed state of ASH1-modified chromatin is largely contingent upon the presence of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me.
source: The repressed state of ASH1-modified chromatin is largely contingent upon the presence of ASH1-catalyzed H3K36me
evidence: This is inferred from RNA-seq data showing derepression of ASH1-marked genes in the ash1(Y888F) mutant.

claim: ASH1-modified chromatin can be further modified with H3K27me2/3 catalyzed by the PRC2 complex to support repression.
source: but can be further modified with H3K27me2/3 catalyzed by the PRC2 complex to support repression
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data showing overlap of ASH1 and H3K27me2/3 marks.
